evidence: tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py docstring: 'It intentionally does NOT fail when a NEW live key is absent from the golden (adding a surface is not a regression); regenerate the golden deliberately when you add one.'

The two live tests (test_no_config_key_removed_without_a_tombstone / test_no_env_var_removed_without_a_tombstone) only iterate `data['config_keys']`/`data['canonical_env_vars']` and flag GOLDEN entries missing from the live schema — never the reverse.
findings.finding: The plan claims the config-surface golden guard fails closed on a NEW live key absent from tests/golden/config_surface.json ('a live key absent here fails tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py'), but that test is removal-only and its docstring explicitly states it does NOT fail when a new live key is absent from the golden.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the caller-side timeout-detection step: the renderer arms proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s) and, on TimeoutExpired, invokes reap_process_group — the shared helper reaps but does not itself enforce the wall-clock bound.
evidence: _proc.py:77-90 reap_process_group only kills/drains; it does not wait for the timeout
acli_subprocess.py:387-397 caller does p.communicate(timeout=call_timeout) then _reap_process_group(p) on TimeoutExpired
findings.finding: The plan implies passing the Popen to reap_process_group achieves the wall-clock timeout, but the verified helper only performs the reap AFTER a timeout is detected — the timeout itself must be enforced by the renderer's own proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s) / except TimeoutExpired, exactly as the ACLI caller does. The plan does not name this caller-side timeout-detection step.
findings.location: Approach — timeout/reaping paragraph; Acceptance Criteria line 1
scenarios: Implementer wires only the reaper and never arms a timeout, so a pathological pandoc still hangs indefinitely

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Establish and test that a combined contiguous-safe-run render is lossless/equivalent to 271c's per-unit rendering at unit joins — name a batching-equivalence corpus assertion (combined-run wiki == concatenation of per-unit renders) so batching cannot re-introduce corruption the per-unit path avoided.

findings.finding: The plan changes pandoc's input granularity from 271c's per-unit rendering to a per-safe-RUN combined Markdown document, but does not establish that rendering a concatenated safe run is lossless/equivalent to 271c's validated per-unit rendering at the unit joins.

scenarios: A safe run where a reference-style link definition in one unit is consumed by prose in an adjacent unit

findings.suggested_fix: Add a Testing item and AC asserting, over the vendored DC corpus, that the combined safe-run wiki equals the concatenation of the corresponding per-unit renders; if any join diverges, either fall back to per-unit rendering for that run or exclude the divergent boundary from batching.
